answers.core:
I think this should be core because other game engines like Unreal Engine have this functionality but also, is a must for certain SFX which are not possible without SDF textures.

Also, the naming is not intuitive and could potentially be extended to other types of textures and such.
answers.workaround:
It can be worked around but requires you to do a lot and is not intuitive. You would have to bake the texture through code and pass the texture into a shader to then utilize it conditionally for many shader SFX. 

The issues:

- The name of the node is not intuitive
- The engine doesn't give you another way to create/bake SDF textures
- The engine doesn't let you create SDF textures on mesh import
- The engine doesn't let you access SDF textures natively in the shader

title: Break up GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D into more generalized GPUTextureBaker3D node
